body:
With NX8's 8-bit static formats, the tensor that loses most even in its best format is layernorm output in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256: 32.1 dB SQNR (signal-to-quantization-noise ratio; higher is better) in fp8_e2m5, measured on that tensor alone by the format search. Measured on 7 models with a format search (of 281 surveyed).

Model outputs keep a median 23.2 dB SQNR against full precision, the worst 12.8 dB (stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5:vae). 5 of 7 models with a prediction metric (top-1, perplexity or agreement) lose some of it; the most: stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5:vae (token agreement 100% → 66%: the share of token positions whose predicted token matches full precision's), facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (token agreement 100% → 67%: the share of token positions whose predicted token matches full precision's) and openai-community/gpt2 (perplexity 43.3 → 48.4, higher is worse).

The tensors that lose most in their best format (their own error): layernorm output in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (fp8_e2m5, 32.1 dB), add output in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (fp8_e2m5, 34.0 dB), layernorm bias in jonatasgrosman/wav2vec2-large-xlsr-53-japanese (fp8_e3m4, 34.2 dB), mul output in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (fp8_e2m5, 34.5 dB), layernorm bias in openai-community/gpt2 (fp8_e3m4, 34.5 dB), linear bias in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5 (fp8_e2m5, 34.7 dB), layernorm output in jonatasgrosman/wav2vec2-large-xlsr-53-japanese (fp8_e3m4, 35.5 dB), linear output in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (fp8_e2m5, 35.5 dB), linear output in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5 (fp8_e3m4, 35.8 dB) and groupnorm bias in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5 (fp8_e2m5, 35.8 dB).

Separately, the error accumulated along the data path (every tensor before a node quantized too): mul outputs end furthest from full precision, facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 keeping only -0.8 dB there. The outputs furthest from full precision in each model's best format set: mul in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (fp8_e2m5, -0.8 dB), softmax in jonatasgrosman/wav2vec2-large-xlsr-53-japanese (ufp8_e1m7, 1.9 dB), bmm in jonatasgrosman/wav2vec2-large-xlsr-53-japanese (fp8_e2m5, 4.1 dB), linear in jonatasgrosman/wav2vec2-large-xlsr-53-japanese (fp8_e2m5, 4.4 dB), linear in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (fp8_e2m5, 7.6 dB), attention in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (fp8_e2m5, 9.2 dB), linear in mobilevit_s.cvnets_in1k (fp8_e2m5, 9.2 dB), silu in mobilevit_s.cvnets_in1k (fp8_e2m5, 10.5 dB), attention in mobilevit_s.cvnets_in1k (fp8_e2m5, 11.1 dB) and linear in google/vit-base-patch16-224 (fp8_e3m4, 11.3 dB).

Formats chosen (E = exponent bits, M = mantissa bits, u = unsigned): fp8_e2m5 3943 (73%), fp8_e1m6 941 (17%), fp8_e3m4 478 (8.84%), ufp8_e2m6 44 (0.81%), ufp8_e3m5 2 (0.04%), ufp8_e1m7 2 (0.04%); 0.89% of tensors use an unsigned format.

A wider format or a per-row choice would recover most where an output's own error in its format, times its data, is largest: silu in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5:vae (fp8_e2m5, 42.4 dB), conv2d in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5:vae (fp8_e1m6, 43.4 dB) and upsample in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5:vae (fp8_e1m6, 43.9 dB).

body:
2 missing capabilities keep 31 operations in 3 models (of 7 planned) off the chip's direct path; the most widespread is run-time addressing (a load from an address computed on chip) (30 operations in 2 models). Ranked by the MACs they hold:

**Run-time addressing (a load from an address computed on chip).** The chip cannot read memory at an address computed at run time, so every lookup or choice by a run-time value (embedding) needs a workaround. It affects 30 operations in 2 models: 30 calls (1.02% of all calls) and no MACs (data movement only); the biggest: embedding in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 and embedding in openai-community/gpt2. Cost today: 0 of 30 have a workaround (0 exact, 0 approximate), 0 failed and 30 wait for one; 0 workarounds proposed, 0 passing its check, none evaluated on a model; accuracy not measured yet; cycles not measured yet; 0 extra kernels.

**An aten::conv1d instruction.** The chip has no instruction for aten::conv1d, so every aten::conv1d needs a workaround. It affects 1 operation in 1 model: 1 call (0.03% of all calls) and MACs not counted (the capture does not size an ATen op); the biggest: aten::conv1d in jonatasgrosman/wav2vec2-large-xlsr-53-japanese. title: Missing instructions: 31 operations in 3 models need workarounds

body:
A kernel reads a tensor in the arrangement its writer stored it in; when the reader needs another arrangement, the reading kernel has to rearrange the data itself. This happens to 528 of 867 tensors passed between kernels (61%) in 7 models: 351 for attention heads split or merged, 157 for other reshapes, 17 for pixels reordered and 3 for image patches.

The reading operations are 342 operations (342 calls, 12% of all calls; 101 G MACs, 4.16% of all MACs). The most common causes (writer → reader): linear → attention (attention heads split or merged) 207, linear → bmm (attention heads split or merged) 144 and linear → add (other reshapes) 58; most in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (196), stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5 (128) and jonatasgrosman/wav2vec2-large-xlsr-53-japanese (87).

Cost today: extra cycles not measured yet (no reading kernel has run); 0 links fail.
title: Layout conversions: 528 of 867 tensors between kernels are rearranged

body:
Activations such as exp, GELU and reciprocal go through a 256-entry lookup table (LUT), which limits their precision: 867 operations in 7 models (867 calls, 29% of all calls), most often layernorm (233), silu (210) and groupnorm (113). Their quantized accuracy: worst 1.9 dB SQNR over 867 measured operations.

Kernels per forward pass (host launches, one per planned kernel call): median 41, most 81 (stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5, 81 planned groups), over 7 models.

FP32 headroom (how far the largest value is from FP32 overflow, in powers of ten) is least at 33.4 powers of ten for bmm in jonatasgrosman/wav2vec2-large-xlsr-53-japanese (largest value 1.35e+05).

13 outputs in 1 model hold a value at the FP32 limit itself (mostly add (12) and select_where (1), e.g. an attention mask's fill value); they are counted apart from the headroom.

Instruction memory (IMEM, 1,024 words per bank) use: not measured yet (no kernel built).
title: Resource limits: 867 operations limited by the LUT and up to 81 kernel launches per pass

body:
**IPU architecture costs, most costly first:**

1. **Compute efficiency is unmeasured** — no kernel has been built, so MAC utilisation is unknown, and instruction memory use is likewise unmeasured.

2. **Accuracy loss under NX8 formats** — with 8-bit static formats, model outputs lose a median 22.6 dB SQNR (worst 12.8 dB), 4 of 5 models lose prediction quality (e.g. GPT-2 perplexity 43.3 → 71.2, DiT and SD-VAE token agreement drop to ~67%), and the worst tensors are layernorm/add/mul outputs in DiT (32–35 dB in their best format); accumulated along the data path, mul outputs in DiT fall to −0.8 dB.

3. **Resource limits** — 550 operations (28% of calls, mostly silu, layernorm, attention) are constrained by a 256-entry LUT with worst 9.2 dB SQNR; forward passes need a median 58 kernel launches (up to 81), and 13 outputs in DiT sit at the FP32 limit.

4. **Layout conversions** — 61% of inter-kernel tensors (357 of 583) must be rearranged by the reading kernel, affecting 219 calls (11%) holding 14% of MACs, mostly for attention head split/merge (linear → attention, 207 cases).

5. **Missing instructions** — 29 calls (1.48%, data movement only, no MACs) in DiT need run-time addressing the chip lacks; none has a workaround yet, so their accuracy and cycle cost are unmeasured, though adding the capability would let all 29 run directly.
title: GLM summary

body:
**Run-time addressing (a load from an address computed on chip)** would put 30 operations in 2 models on the chip directly, with no workaround: 30 calls (1.02% of all calls) and no MACs (they only move data); the accuracy it would recover is not measured yet (no workaround evaluated).

**An aten::conv1d instruction** would put 1 operation in 1 model on the chip directly, with no workaround: 1 call (0.03% of all calls) and MACs not counted (the capture does not size an ATen op); the accuracy it would recover is not measured yet (no workaround evaluated).
